# Frade — Engineering Agent Contract

## Purpose

This file defines repository-wide engineering rules for AI coding agents working on Frade.

These rules are mandatory.

Subsystem-specific rules may exist in nested `AGENTS.md` files and may impose stricter constraints.

---

## 1. Development Method

Frade uses:

```text
SDD / OpenSpec
    ↓
BDD
    ↓
TDD
    ↓
Implementation
    ↓
Verification
    ↓
Architecture Gate
    ↓
Archive
```

Implementation follows specification.

Specification must not be silently changed to match implementation.

Tests must not be weakened to make implementation pass.

---

## 2. OpenSpec Is the Change Authority

For substantial product or architecture work:

1. identify the active OpenSpec change;
2. read its proposal/spec/design/tasks;
3. validate the change before implementation;
4. implement only the active scope;
5. run required tests;
6. run OpenSpec verification;
7. pass the Architecture Gate;
8. only then archive the change.

Do not implement a later dependent change before the previous change has passed its gate.

---

## 3. STOP Conditions

Stop progression whenever any of the following is true:

```text
required test fails
typecheck fails in affected code
OpenSpec validation fails
OpenSpec verification has a correctness blocker
architecture invariant fails
architecture gate fails
reference parity fails
a specification conflict exists
a previously fixed regression reappears
```

Resolve the blocker before moving to the next phase.

---

## 4. No Patch-Loop Rule

After two unsuccessful fixes of the same deterministic defect:

```text
STOP PATCHING
```

Before another production-code modification, perform root-cause analysis.

Classify the failure as:

```text
DOMAIN_MODEL
INVARIANT
ALGORITHM
ABSTRACTION_BOUNDARY
STATE_TRANSITION
TEST
SPEC_CONFLICT
INTEGRATION
ENVIRONMENT
```

Do not continue making local symptom-oriented fixes.

---

## 5. Regression-First Rule

For a reproduced defect use:

```text
DEFECT
 ↓
DETERMINISTIC REPRODUCTION
 ↓
FAILING TEST / FIXTURE
 ↓
ROOT CAUSE
 ↓
IMPLEMENTATION FIX
 ↓
TARGETED TEST
 ↓
FULL REGRESSION SUITE
```

Do not fix production code first and add a regression test afterwards unless reproduction before the fix is technically impossible and explicitly documented.

---

## 6. Test Integrity

Do not make tests pass by weakening them.

Forbidden without an explicit specification decision:

```text
test.skip
it.skip
describe.skip

test.only
it.only
describe.only

removing meaningful assertions
loosening geometry tolerances
blind snapshot regeneration
deleting regression fixtures
ignoring thrown errors
changing expected values merely to match current implementation
@ts-nocheck
@ts-ignore
```

Existing regression tests are historical evidence.

Do not remove them casually.

---

## 7. Architecture Direction

Prefer dependency direction:

```text
UI / Framework
      ↓
Adapters
      ↓
Application / Interaction
      ↓
Domain
      ↓
Pure primitives
```

Do not solve domain defects inside renderers, React lifecycle hooks, persistence adapters, or framework glue.

Fix the first incorrect decision in the proper layer.

---

## 8. Derived State

Do not persist state that can be deterministically derived from semantic state unless the specification explicitly requires materialization.

Typical transient/derived state includes:

```text
selection handles
preview geometry
render-only paths
cached projections
temporary interaction coordinates
```

---

## 9. Determinism

Core domain algorithms must not depend on accidental runtime state such as:

```text
Math.random()
Date.now()
DOM ordering
React render ordering
screen zoom
devicePixelRatio
pointer event frequency
animation-frame timing
```

Identical semantic inputs must produce identical semantic outputs within the explicitly defined numeric tolerance.

---

## 10. Scope Discipline

Do not turn an active OpenSpec change into an unrelated repository-wide refactoring.

If unrelated technical debt is discovered:

```text
document it
do not opportunistically implement it
```

unless it blocks the active change.

---

## 11. Evidence

Never report:

```text
"should pass"
"looks correct"
"probably fixed"
```

as verification.

Claims about passing tests or validation must come from commands that were actually executed.

At the end of implementation report:

```text
CHANGE:
IMPLEMENTED:
FILES CHANGED:
TESTS ADDED:
COMMANDS EXECUTED:
TEST RESULTS:
KNOWN BLOCKERS:
READY_FOR_VERIFY: YES | NO
```

---

## 12. Architecture Gate

An Architecture Gate is a review phase.

During a gate:

```text
DO NOT MODIFY PRODUCTION CODE
```

unless the task is explicitly changed from review to repair.

Gate output must contain exactly one unambiguous status:

```text
GATE_STATUS: PASS
```

or:

```text
GATE_STATUS: FAIL
```

Correctness or architecture blockers always mean `FAIL`.

---

## 13. No Autonomous Phase Advancement

Do not automatically start the next numbered OpenSpec change after completing the current one.

Example:

```text
R04 complete
→ STOP
→ report status
```

Do not automatically begin R05.

Each numbered change is an engineering checkpoint.

---

## 14. Routing Engine V2

Any task involving:

```text
edge routing
edge connections
terminal attachment
waypoints
orthogonal routing
segment editing
routing preview
self-loops
routing rendering
routing/X6 integration
```

must additionally read:

```text
docs/routing-v2/drawio-routing-master-spec.md
docs/routing-v2/implementation-playbook.md
```

These documents define the Routing Engine V2 architecture and implementation program.

When a routing-specific nested `AGENTS.md` exists, its stricter rules also apply.

Do not implement Routing Engine V2 from memory or from legacy code alone.

---

## 15. Routing V2 Sequence

Routing Engine V2 follows this dependency order:

```text
R01 Geometry Kernel
 ↓
R02 Terminal / Perimeter
 ↓
R03 Direction Resolver
 ↓
R04 Orthogonal Router
 ↓
R05 Segment Router
 ↓
R06 Segment Editor
 ↓
R07 Preview / Commit
 ↓
R08 Self-loop
 ↓
R09 Draw.io Differential Harness
 ↓
R10 X6 Integration
```

A later change must not compensate for a defect in an earlier layer.

Fix the responsible layer.

---

## 16. Git Safety

Do not perform destructive operations merely to simplify implementation.

Do not execute without explicit instruction:

```text
git reset --hard
git clean -fd
discard unrelated user changes
rewrite unrelated commits
```

Before reporting implementation complete, inspect:

```text
git status
git diff
```

Unexpected unrelated changes must be identified.

---

## 17. Prime Directive

Do not optimize for:

```text
"make the current visual symptom disappear"
```

Optimize for:

```text
correct domain model
+
explicit invariants
+
deterministic implementation
+
executable regression protection
+
correct architecture boundary
```

---

## 18. Independent Feature Ownership and Parallel Work

The active change is selected for the current task and workspace. A program's
`CURRENT_CHANGE.md`, phase, frozen fingerprints and numbered sequence govern work
in that program; they are not a repository-wide lock on independent features.
Sections 1–17 remain mandatory. A failing applicable check still stops its owner.

Independent features may proceed in parallel in separate branches/worktrees.
Each has its own approved scope, baseline, PRE, tests, verification, POST and
archive checkpoint. Do not run concurrent writers in the same checkout. Do not

1	# Proposal
     2	
     3	## Why
     4	
     5	Diagram colors currently appear inside theme-dependent editing chrome, so changing the application theme can change the viewing context. The user approved one shared light editing environment for Draw.io and Frade, preserving authored paint and Windows forced-colors precedence.
     6	
     7	## What Changes
     8	
     9	- Add a fixed, derived light presentation scope for both diagram editors: canvas, editor toolbars, palettes, format panels, flow/reference panels, menus, dialogs, tooltips and editor-owned overlays, including portals outside the editor DOM subtree.
    10	- Keep the external workbench, editor-group tabs, application Settings and global theme picker on the selected application theme. Both density choices remain independent.
    11	- Use one shared editor role projection from existing Frade Light tokens, with canvas `#F9FAFC` and decorative dot color `#CDD3DC`. Preserve authored page backgrounds/images over the neutral workspace.
    12	- Preserve exact authored fill/stroke/text/opacity/gradient attributes and their palette previews. No automatic inversion, tint, theme-driven attribute replacement or document rewrite. Windows forced colors is the explicit system-controlled display exception.
    13	- **BREAKING visual contract:** diagram-owned UI no longer follows Dark/HC/System/reference colors or the reference geometry preset when forced colors is inactive. Global theme identity and transaction revision remain unchanged.
    14	- Establish common appearance/interaction measurements for comparable controls in both engines without claiming support for identical feature sets or universal pixel parity.
    15	
    16	## Capabilities
    17	
    18	### New Capabilities
    19	
    20	- `diagram-editor-presentation`: stable light editing scope, ownership of nested/portaled surfaces, authored-paint fidelity and cross-engine presentation parity.
    21	
    22	### Modified Capabilities
    23	
    24	- `theme-core`: make local diagram presentation explicit while preserving atomic revision/ACK/rollback and document isolation.
    25	- `workbench-visual-contract`: delimit reference geometry to the external workbench and require shared light diagram-editor measurements.
    26	- `bundled-reference-themes`: disclose the local editor exception to reference fidelity and default-appearance restoration.
    27	
    28	## Impact
    29	
    30	Planning owner: `codex/frade-light-diagram-editor`, clean baseline `4244e5668e50f74b9b536c2f0ffc44c56279e945`. Existing shared theme adapters, Draw.io bridge and native editor roots are the implementation boundaries; see design.md for the explicit allowlist. No new UI library, resolver, persisted setting or dependency is proposed. P02-P07, routing/domain/vendor sources, branding and historical evidence remain outside scope. PRE and POST use exactly `gpt-6-sol` / `xhigh`, automatically under the existing confined review service.

     2	
     3	## Context
     4	
     5	See proposal.md for motivation. Baseline is Main `4244e5668e50f74b9b536c2f0ffc44c56279e945`; this branch contains no uncommitted P02/Routing code. Root AGENTS sections 18-22 and Guide v1.0 apply. No nested AGENTS exists in the affected UI/desktop paths; routing-scoped rules are outside this presentation change.

     7	Observed boundaries:
     8	- `nativeParticipant.ts` projects snapshot diagram.canvas/grid through existing X6 view managers. It does not own cells or persistence.
     9	- `frameParticipant.ts` authenticates phase/owner and waits for painted ACK; `drawio-theme-bridge.ts` applies frame CSS plus a private SVG dot grid. The bridge currently derives color-scheme from the application snapshot.
    10	- `DiagramView.tsx` and `FradeDiagramView.tsx` portal their content into retained editor containers. Both have breadcrumbs/actions, reference controls, flow manager, readonly/error states and local reconnect UI.
    11	- `rootParticipant.ts` validates the complete 31-role DTO, projects system colors and applies the ID-derived reference preset. The application snapshot must not be mutated to make one editor light.
    12	- `overlays.ts` supplies stable host, modal priority, inert/focus/Escape handling; it has no diagram appearance-owner field today.
    13	- `DiagramEditor.tsx` contains the native toolbar, existing grid visibility and a standalone name prompt fallback. Its embedded desktop path hides the standalone toolbar/name-prompt fallback. Its routing/selection handlers are not appearance repair points.
    14	
    15	Inventory and exact raw hashes are recorded in evidence/planning/inventory.json. Prior archived visual PASS, 372 P01 images and 19 reference images remain historical, not baselines for this change.
    16	
    17	## Goals / Non-Goals
    18	
    19	**Goals:** one shared editor light projection; complete editor-owned surface coverage; faithful supported authored paint; same comparable control metrics; truthful forced-colors behavior; no flash on bootstrap/restore; unchanged atomic transaction and accessibility guarantees.
    20	
    21	**Non-Goals:** changing application defaults/selection, adding a light-editor setting, a second resolver/UI library/icon family, rewriting vendor files, synchronizing diagram formats or feature sets, changing author styling/persistence/export, snap/routing/endpoints, P02-P07 or a general UI migration. OS-owned titlebars, file/color chooser windows and browser-native prompts are outside application-rendered styling; any reachable native prompt must be identified as system UI, not falsely counted as a themed application dialog.
    22	
    23	## Decisions
    24	
    25	### 1. One derived scope after the existing resolver
    26	
    27	Add `packages/ui-workspace/src/design/theme/editorPresentation.ts` as a pure view projection from a validated ResolvedTheme. Use the canonical built-in Light palette, independent density and the original transaction revision. Ignore application theme/user color overrides only within this explicitly fixed editor scope. Do not select/persist another theme or mutate registry/input. For ordinary HC selection with forced colors inactive, the editor is still light, as explicitly accepted by the user. Forced colors is the sole palette exception and retains the existing final system mapping.
    28	
    29	The derived snapshot may identify the built-in Light palette locally; the authoritative application ID/kind/settings stay in the existing controller. Service contexts, session/generation/membership, transaction IDs, revision, READY/PAINTED guards, cancellation, one bounded membership reprepare and 2s/5s deadlines remain exact. Never spoof a global ID or send a light palette with a dark DTO kind to bypass validation.
    30	
    31	Project only at editor participant boundaries. Give each complete diagram editor container an owned light root. Compose its root work with the existing native/frame presentation participant under the same registration/paint barrier where possible; do not create an asynchronously updated CSS subscription that misses preview or reveals before ACK. Parent editor chrome and iframe/native canvas must both be prepared before reveal. Global overlays and the recovery curtain keep existing application/system ownership.
    32	
    33	### 2. Canonical roles and geometry
    34	
    35	Reuse canonical Light surface/text/action/border/status/focus roles and existing density values: compact controls/rows 28px, comfortable 36px, coarse targets 44px, focus stroke 2px, common control radius 4px. Normal text >=4.5:1 and meaningful control/state graphics >=3:1 are tested against actual backdrops. Palette/style samples are content paint, not control foreground.
    36	
    37	Keep canonical tokens.json and generated token artifacts byte-identical in this stage: their adoption oracle allows only the historic single-selector exception. Instead add versioned `packages/ui-workspace/tokens/diagram-editor-presentation.json` as a narrowly scoped role profile referencing canonical Light roles, with only neutral canvas #F9FAFC and decorative grid #CDD3DC declared there. This is role data, not feature-level literals or another resolver. Validate its allowed keys, HEX values and provenance in the existing UI test/compliance chain; include an isolated negative profile and palette/scope-leak regression. Global theme definitions and all three built-in role sets stay unchanged.
    38	
    39	Match visible dots across engines at scale 1 using the existing Draw.io radius 0.6 (1.2px diameter), same configured semantic grid phase and color. Preserve the current semantic grid size (normally 10), visibility preference, snap and view transforms. Do not implement the research suggestion of a new 20px/adaptive grid algorithm here. Explicit page backgrounds/images remain above the neutral workspace and remain export-owned content.
    40	
    41	The VS Code preset remains applicable only to external workbench controls. Editor roots/owned overlays reset reference-only color/metric variables explicitly through the scoped shared style; no broad `all:unset`, filter/inversion or new arbitrary CSS execution.
    42	
    43	### 3. Explicit appearance ownership
    44	
    45	Use an editor-instance ownership lease for each retained editor root and its application-rendered overlays, with exact teardown/reassignment. Scope by owning editor, never by global screen coordinates or every dialog/menu in the document. Keep the existing single managed overlay host and keyboard/modal ordering. A portaled editor dialog/menu can remain positioned by its existing host while receiving the editor's shared light role scope. Disposal and editor switch remove only owned attributes/styles and cannot restyle another editor or the global theme picker. For a dirty guard originating from exactly one diagram key, the presentation ask helper may resolve that existing draft repository/path to exactly one live retained root inside this Workbench and capture its opaque lease at prompt creation. Unknown/multiple/document-object origins remain explicitly workspace-owned; a supplied stale/foreign lease must fail rather than silently rebind to another editor. Focus/active-tab/coordinates are not ownership evidence. Existing dirty guard actions and modal priority/focus handling stay unchanged. Owner-projected snapshots update registered portaled roots synchronously in the same composite apply/rollback under the existing cover; disposal restores only owned projection fields.
    46	
    47	Inside the pinned Draw.io iframe, owned chrome includes menubar, toolbar, sidebar/library palette, format panel, footer/page tabs, native Draw.io popup/submenu/dialog and tooltip roots. Broad text/control rules must exclude author color swatches, SVG thumbnails and style preview content. Preserve existing positively owned icon resources/handlers and current keyboard/focus leases; unknown glyphs are not silently recolored by hash allowlisting. Track popup/tooltip creation within the verified iframe and restore only bridge-owned presentation. Native X6 SVG cell attributes remain outside UI CSS selectors.
    48	
    49	### 4. Author paint and supported parity
    50	
    51	No calls to graph/model style mutation, setBackgroundColor, page setters, adaptive color toggles that write a document, import/export normalization or repository appearance mutation from a theme transaction. Compare before/after JSON/XML bytes plus dirty state, undo, selections, cells, editor/iframe identities and authored backgrounds. UI focus/selection handles remain overlays distinct from authored stroke/fill.
    52	
    53	Use actual supported `elementAppearance.ts`/Draw.io appearance adapters as read-only witnesses. The native document schema has no page-background/image or gradient fields; those witnesses are Draw.io-only, and no unsupported native feature is invented. For shared opaque fill/stroke/text, compare source values, computed SVG/canvas paint and palette data. For opacity and gradients, compare composited samples over the same declared backing color; identical HEX alone is insufficient. Images retain source/opacity. Inherited/default styles are tested for stable effective appearance without materializing new persisted attributes. A feature absent in either engine is reported UNSUPPORTED/NOT_APPLICABLE with evidence; no invented feature or universal pixel-perfect claim.
    54	
    55	### 5. Formal conflict resolution
    56	
    57	User authority is recorded in decisions/accepted-scope.md. The deltas explicitly modify theme-core atomic/isolation scenarios, workbench reference-geometry scope and bundled-reference fidelity boundaries. During implementation publish an approved-scope companion at docs/ui/diagram-editor-presentation.md, explicitly documenting the exception to Guide 5.1 and Themes-and-Plugins Spec section 6: ordinary app light/dark/HC still ship together, but these two diagram editors use the shared Light scope, with Windows forced colors final. Interpret FDS-003/008 as reuse of one shared scoped system, not independent engine palettes. Do not edit historical archives or declare the old gate automatically accepting the new appearance.

    17	## Goals / Non-Goals

    25	### 1. One derived scope after the existing resolver
    26

    30	
    31	Project only at editor participant boundaries. Give each complete diagram editor container an owned light root. A portaled editor dialog/menu can remain positioned by its existing host while receiving the editor's shared light role scope. Disposal and editor switch remove only owned attributes/styles and cannot restyle another editor or the global theme picker. For a dirty guard originating from exactly one diagram key, the presentation ask helper may resolve that existing draft repository/path to exactly one live retained root inside this Workbench and capture its opaque lease at prompt creation. Unknown/multiple/document-object origins remain explicitly workspace-owned; a supplied stale/foreign lease must fail rather than silently rebind to another editor. Focus/active-tab/coordinates are not ownership evidence. Existing dirty guard actions and modal priority/focus handling stay unchanged. Owner-projected snapshots update registered portaled roots synchronously in the same composite apply/rollback under the existing cover; disposal restores only owned projection fields.

docs/ui/Frade-UI-Style-Guide.md:110:### 5.1 Токены и темы
docs/ui/Frade-UI-Style-Guide.md:129:Темы: пользователь выбирает light / dark / high-contrast / system. В system приложение наблюдает изменения системной темы; явный выбор имеет приоритет. В `forced-colors` применяются системные цвета, включая SVG и подписи холста. Canvas-рендерер MUST получать отдельный доступный mapping и альтернативное представление; CSS-переменных для DOM недостаточно. docs/ui/Frade-UI-Style-Guide.md:245:Холст: нейтральный `diagram.canvas`, малоконтрастная сетка по настройке, ясное выделение, стабильная геометрия. docs/ui/Frade-UI-Style-Guide.md:263:Сообщения — спокойные текстовые блоки с явным автором и действиями, без ярких messenger-bubbles. Ширина чтения по умолчанию до 760; центрирование внутри широкой editor group. Код — mono, копирование и горизонтальная прокрутка. Composer имеет видимый режим/placeholder, attach controls, выбранную модель, send/stop. Отправка по умолчанию Enter, Shift+Enter — перенос; настройка Ctrl+Enter MUST быть доступна и показываться в подсказке. Нельзя отправлять сообщение при незавершённом IME composition.
